clusters.name: Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems

standards.description: Use units to understand and guide solutions; choose and interpret units in formulas, graphs, and data displays.
standards.ccssText: Use units as a way to understand problems and to guide the solution of multi-step problems; choose and interpret units consistently in formulas; choose and interpret the scale and the origin in graphs and data displays. (N-Q.A.1)

standards.description: Define appropriate quantities to describe and model a real-world situation.
standards.ccssText: Define appropriate quantities for the purpose of descriptive modeling. (N-Q.A.2)

standards.description: Choose a level of accuracy appropriate to the limitations of measurement when reporting quantities.
standards.ccssText: Choose a level of accuracy appropriate to limitations on measurement when reporting quantities. (N-Q.A.3)

standards.description: Interpret parts of an expression, including terms, factors, coefficients, and complex sub-expressions, in context.
standards.ccssText: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context. (A-SSE.A.1)

subStandards.description: Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients.
Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity.

standards.description: Use the structure of an expression to identify and apply ways to rewrite it into an equivalent form.
standards.ccssText: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it. (A-SSE.A.2)

clusters.name: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems

standards.description: Choose and produce an equivalent form of an expression to reveal and explain properties of the quantity it represents.
standards.ccssText: Choose and produce an equivalent form of an expression to reveal and explain properties of the quantity represented by the expression. (A-SSE.B.3)

subStandards.description: Factor a quadratic expression to reveal the zeros of the function it defines.
Complete the square in a quadratic expression to reveal the maximum or minimum value of the function it defines.
Use the properties of exponents to transform expressions for exponential functions.

domains.name: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions

standards.description: Add, subtract, and multiply polynomials, understanding that polynomials are closed under these operations like integers.
standards.ccssText: Understand that polynomials form a system analogous to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and multiplication; add, subtract, and multiply polynomials. (A-APR.A.1)

clusters.name: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships

standards.skillName: Equations and Inequalities in One Variable
standards.description: Create equations and inequalities in one variable to model and solve problems from linear, quadratic, rational, and exponential contexts.
standards.ccssText: Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear and quadratic functions, and simple rational and exponential functions. (A-CED.A.1)

standards.skillName: Equations in Two or More Variables
standards.description: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships, and graph them on coordinate axes with appropriate labels and scales.
standards.ccssText: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales. (A-CED.A.2)

standards.description: Represent constraints using equations, inequalities, or systems, and interpret solutions as viable or non-viable in a modeling context.
standards.ccssText: Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or non-viable options in a modeling context. (A-CED.A.3)

standards.description: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest using the same reasoning as solving equations.
standards.ccssText: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations. (A-CED.A.4)

clusters.name: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning

standards.description: Explain each step in solving a simple equation as following from equality, and construct an argument to justify the solution method.
standards.ccssText: Explain each step in solving a simple equation as following from the equality of numbers asserted at the previous step, starting from the assumption that the original equation has a solution. Construct a viable argument to justify a solution method. (A-REI.A.1)

clusters.name: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable

standards.description: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including those with letter coefficients.
standards.ccssText: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with coefficients represented by letters. (A-REI.B.3)

standards.description: Solve quadratic equations in one variable using multiple methods including completing the square, the quadratic formula, and factoring.
standards.ccssText: Solve quadratic equations in one variable. (A-REI.B.4)

subStandards.description: Use the method of completing the square to transform any quadratic equation in x into an equation of the form (x - p)^2 = q that has the same solutions.
Solve quadratic equations by inspection (e.g., for x^2 = 49), taking square roots, completing the square, the quadratic formula and factoring, as appropriate to the initial form of the equation.

standards.description: Prove that replacing one equation in a system with the sum of that equation and a multiple of another yields a system with the same solutions.
standards.ccssText: Prove that, given a system of two equations in two variables, replacing one equation by the sum of that equation and a multiple of the other produces a system with the same solutions. (A-REI.C.5)

standards.description: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately, focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables.
standards.ccssText: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately (e.g., with graphs), focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables. (A-REI.C.6)

clusters.name: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically

standards.description: Understand that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate plane.
standards.ccssText: Understand that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate plane, often forming a curve (which could be a line). (A-REI.D.10)

standards.description: Explain why x-coordinates of intersections of y = f(x) and y = g(x) are solutions of f(x) = g(x), and find solutions approximately using technology.
standards.ccssText: Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect are the solutions of the equation f(x) = g(x); find the solutions approximately, e.g., using technology to graph the functions, make tables of values, or find successive approximations. (A-REI.D.11)

standards.description: Graph the solution set of a linear inequality or system of linear inequalities in two variables as a half-plane or intersection of half-planes.
standards.ccssText: Graph the solutions to a linear inequality in two variables as a half-plane (excluding the boundary in the case of a strict inequality), and graph the solution set to a system of linear inequalities in two variables as the intersection of the corresponding half-planes. (A-REI.D.12)

clusters.name: Understand the concept of a function and use function notation

standards.description: Understand that a function assigns exactly one output to each input, and that the graph of f is the graph of y = f(x).
standards.ccssText: Understand that a function from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the range) assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range. If f is a function and x is an element of its domain, then f(x) denotes the output of f corresponding to the input x. The graph of f is the graph of the equation y = f(x). (F-IF.A.1)

standards.description: Use function notation, evaluate functions for given inputs, and interpret function notation statements in context.
standards.ccssText: Use function notation, evaluate functions for inputs in their domains, and interpret statements that use function notation in terms of a context. (F-IF.A.2)

standards.description: Recognize that sequences are functions with a domain that is a subset of integers, and may be defined recursively.
standards.ccssText: Recognize that sequences are functions, sometimes defined recursively, whose domain is a subset of the integers. (F-IF.A.3)

clusters.name: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context

standards.description: Interpret key features of graphs and tables of functions modeling two quantities, and sketch graphs from verbal descriptions.
standards.ccssText: For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal description of the relationship. (F-IF.B.4)

standards.description: Relate the domain of a function to its graph and to the quantitative relationship it describes.
standards.ccssText: Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes. (F-IF.B.5)

standards.description: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function over an interval from a symbolic expression, table, or graph.
standards.ccssText: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph. (F-IF.B.6)

standards.description: Graph functions expressed symbolically showing key features, by hand for simple cases and using technology for complex ones.
standards.ccssText: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases. (F-IF.C.7)

subStandards.description: Graph linear and quadratic functions and show intercepts, maxima, and minima.
Graph square root, cube root, and piecewise-defined functions, including step functions and absolute value functions.
Graph exponential and logarithmic functions, showing intercepts and end behavior.

standards.description: Write a function in different but equivalent forms to reveal and explain different properties of the function.
standards.ccssText: Write a function defined by an expression in different but equivalent forms to reveal and explain different properties of the function. (F-IF.C.8)

subStandards.description: Use the process of factoring and completing the square in a quadratic function to show zeros, extreme values, and symmetry of the graph.
Use the properties of exponents to interpret expressions for exponential functions.

standards.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way, such as algebraically, graphically, in a table, or by verbal description.
standards.ccssText: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions). (F-IF.C.9)

clusters.name: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities

standards.description: Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities using explicit expressions, recursive processes, or arithmetic operations on standard types.
standards.ccssText: Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities. (F-BF.A.1)

subStandards.description: Determine an explicit expression, a recursive process, or steps for calculation from a context.
Combine standard function types using arithmetic operations.

standards.description: Write arithmetic and geometric sequences recursively and explicitly, use them to model situations, and translate between both forms.
standards.ccssText: Write arithmetic and geometric sequences both recursively and with an explicit formula, use them to model situations, and translate between the two forms. (F-BF.A.2)

clusters.name: Build new functions from existing functions

standards.description: Identify and explain the effect of replacing f(x) with f(x) + k, kf(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) on a graph for specific values of k.
standards.ccssText: Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, k f(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) for specific values of k (both positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. Experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph using technology. (F-BF.B.3)

clusters.name: Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems

standards.description: Distinguish situations modeled by linear functions from those modeled by exponential functions, including by rate of change.
standards.ccssText: Distinguish between situations that can be modeled with linear functions and with exponential functions. (F-LE.A.1)

subStandards.description: Prove that linear functions grow by equal differences over equal intervals, and that exponential functions grow by equal factors over equal intervals.
Recognize situations in which one quantity changes at a constant rate per unit interval relative to another.
Recognize situations in which a quantity grows or decays by a constant percent rate per unit interval relative to another.

standards.description: Construct linear and exponential functions from graphs, descriptions, or input-output pairs, including arithmetic and geometric sequences.
standards.ccssText: Construct linear and exponential functions, including arithmetic and geometric sequences, given a graph, a description of a relationship, or two input-output pairs (include reading these from a table). (F-LE.A.2)

standards.description: Observe using graphs and tables that exponential growth eventually exceeds linear, quadratic, or polynomial growth.
standards.ccssText: Observe using graphs and tables that a quantity increasing exponentially eventually exceeds a quantity increasing linearly, quadratically, or (more generally) as a polynomial function. (F-LE.A.3)

clusters.name: Interpret expressions for functions in terms of the situation they model

standards.skillName: Parameters in Linear and Exponential Models
standards.description: Interpret the parameters in a linear or exponential function in terms of the real-world context they model.
standards.ccssText: Interpret the parameters in a linear or exponential function in terms of a context. (F-LE.B.5)

clusters.name: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable

standards.skillName: Data Plots on the Number Line
standards.description: Represent data with dot plots, histograms, and box plots on the real number line.
standards.ccssText: Represent data with plots on the real number line (dot plots, histograms, and box plots). (S-ID.A.1)

standards.description: Use statistics appropriate to the data distribution shape to compare center and spread of two or more data sets.
standards.ccssText: Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distribution to compare center (median, mean) and spread (interquartile range, standard deviation) of two or more different data sets. (S-ID.A.2)

standards.description: Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread of data sets, accounting for the effects of outliers.
standards.ccssText: Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the context of the data sets, accounting for possible effects of extreme data points (outliers). (S-ID.A.3)

clusters.name: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables

standards.description: Summarize categorical data in two-way frequency tables and interpret joint, marginal, and conditional relative frequencies.
standards.ccssText: Summarize categorical data for two categories in two-way frequency tables. Interpret relative frequencies in the context of the data (including joint, marginal, and conditional relative frequencies). Recognize possible associations and trends in the data. (S-ID.B.5)

standards.description: Represent data on a scatter plot, fit a function to the data, and use it to solve problems in context.
standards.ccssText: Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot, and describe how the variables are related. (S-ID.B.6)

subStandards.description: Fit a function to the data; use functions fitted to data to solve problems in the context of the data.
Informally assess the fit of a function by plotting and analyzing residuals.
Fit a linear function for a scatter plot that suggests a linear association.

standards.description: Interpret the slope and y-intercept of a linear model in the context of the data.
standards.ccssText: Interpret the slope (rate of change) and the intercept (constant term) of a linear model in the context of the data. (S-ID.C.7)

standards.description: Compute and interpret the correlation coefficient of a linear fit using technology.
standards.ccssText: Compute (using technology) and interpret the correlation coefficient of a linear fit. (S-ID.C.8)

standards.description: Distinguish between correlation and causation when interpreting data relationships.
standards.ccssText: Distinguish between correlation and causation. (S-ID.C.9)
